label: about
comment: The subject matter of an object.
enriched_comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."
embedding_text: about: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to.

label: abridged
comment: Indicates whether the book is an abridged edition.
enriched_comment: An abridgment status indicating whether a book is a shortened version. Also called shortened, condensed, edited for length. Examples: "An abridged edition of 'Les Misérables' is true.", "An abridged version of 'Moby Dick' is false."
embedding_text: abridged: An abridgment status indicating whether a book is a shortened version. Also called shortened, condensed, edited for length.

label: abstract
comment: An abstract is a short description that summarizes a [[CreativeWork]].
enriched_comment: An abstract relation between a creative work and a short text summarizing its content. Also called summary, synopsis, précis, overview. Examples: "A research paper's abstract describes its findings.", "A movie's abstract outlines its plot."
embedding_text: abstract: An abstract relation between a creative work and a short text summarizing its content. Also called summary, synopsis, précis, overview.

label: accelerationTime
comment:
The time needed to accelerate the vehicle from a given start velocity to a given target velocity.

Typical unit code(s): SEC for seconds

* Note: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for seconds/0..100 km/h or seconds/0..60 mph. Simply use "SEC" for seconds and indicate the velocities in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]], or use [[valueReference]] with a [[QuantitativeValue]] of 0..60 mph or 0..100 km/h to specify the reference speeds.
enriched_comment: An acceleration time relation between a vehicle and the quantitative value representing the time it takes to accelerate between specified velocities. Also called 0-60 mph time, speed-up duration, sprint time. Examples: "A sports car's acceleration time is 3.5 seconds (0-60 mph).", "An electric vehicle's acceleration time is 2.8 seconds (0-100 km/h)."
embedding_text: accelerationTime: An acceleration time relation between a vehicle and the quantitative value representing the time it takes to accelerate between specified velocities. Also called 0-60 mph time, speed-up duration, sprint time.

label: acceptedAnswer
comment: The answer(s) that has been accepted as best, typically on a Question/Answer site. Sites vary in their selection mechanisms, e.g. drawing on community opinion and/or the view of the Question author.
enriched_comment: An accepted answer relation between a question and the answer(s) deemed best or most appropriate. Also called best answer, chosen solution, preferred response. Examples: "A forum question's accepted answer is 'Use a screwdriver'.", "A quiz question's accepted answer is 'Option B'."
embedding_text: acceptedAnswer: An accepted answer relation between a question and the answer(s) deemed best or most appropriate. Also called best answer, chosen solution, preferred response.

label: acceptedOffer
comment: The offer(s) -- e.g., product, quantity and price combinations -- included in the order.
enriched_comment: An accepted offer relation between an order and the specific offer(s) that were agreed upon and included in it. Also called purchased offer, confirmed offer, included offer. Examples: "A customer's order accepted an offer for a laptop.", "The order accepted an offer for two books."
embedding_text: acceptedOffer: An accepted offer relation between an order and the specific offer(s) that were agreed upon and included in it. Also called purchased offer, confirmed offer, included offer.

label: acceptedPaymentMethod
comment: The payment method(s) that are accepted in general by an organization, or for some specific demand or offer.
enriched_comment: An accepted payment method relation between an organization, demand, or offer and the payment methods it allows. Also called payment options, payment types, accepted forms of payment. Examples: "A store accepts credit card payments.", "An online offer accepts PayPal.", "The organization accepts bank transfers."
embedding_text: acceptedPaymentMethod: An accepted payment method relation between an organization, demand, or offer and the payment methods it allows. Also called payment options, payment types, accepted forms of payment.

label: acceptsReservations
comment: Indicates whether a FoodEstablishment accepts reservations. Values can be Boolean, an URL at which reservations can be made or (for backwards compatibility) the strings ```Yes``` or ```No```.
enriched_comment: A reservation acceptance status indicating whether a food establishment allows bookings. Also called takes reservations, booking available, reservation policy. Examples: "A restaurant accepts reservations is true.", "The cafe accepts reservations via its website URL.", "This diner accepts reservations is 'No'."
embedding_text: acceptsReservations: A reservation acceptance status indicating whether a food establishment allows bookings. Also called takes reservations, booking available, reservation policy.

label: accessCode
comment: Password, PIN, or access code needed for delivery (e.g. from a locker).
enriched_comment: An access code relation between a delivery event and the text string required to access the delivered item. Also called delivery PIN, locker code, entry code. Examples: "The package delivery event has an access code '12345'.", "The locker delivery access code is 'PIN6789'."
embedding_text: accessCode: An access code relation between a delivery event and the text string required to access the delivered item. Also called delivery PIN, locker code, entry code.

label: accessMode
comment: The human sensory perceptual system or cognitive faculty through which a person may process or perceive the intellectual content of a resource, not including any adaptations of the content (e.g., text alternatives for images). Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessMode-vocabulary).
enriched_comment: An access mode relation between a creative work and the human sensory or cognitive system through which its content can be perceived. Also called perceptual mode, sensory access, content modality. Examples: "A video's access mode is 'visual'.", "An audiobook's access mode is 'auditory'.", "A text document's access mode is 'textual'."
embedding_text: accessMode: An access mode relation between a creative work and the human sensory or cognitive system through which its content can be perceived. Also called perceptual mode, sensory access, content modality.

label: accessModeSufficient
comment: A list of single or combined access modes that are sufficient to understand all the intellectual content of a resource, including any adaptations. Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessModeSufficient-vocabulary).
enriched_comment: A sufficient access mode relation between a creative work and a list of access modes that are adequate for understanding its full intellectual content. Also called sufficient perceptual modes, adequate access methods. Examples: "A captioned video's sufficient access modes are 'visual' and 'textual'.", "A podcast with a transcript's sufficient access modes are 'auditory' and 'textual'."
embedding_text: accessModeSufficient: A sufficient access mode relation between a creative work and a list of access modes that are adequate for understanding its full intellectual content. Also called sufficient perceptual modes, adequate access methods.

label: accessibilityAPI
comment: Indicates that the resource is compatible with the referenced accessibility API. Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessibilityAPI-vocabulary).
enriched_comment: An accessibility API compatibility relation between a creative work and the accessibility API it supports. Also called API support, accessibility interface. Examples: "A software application's accessibility API is 'AT-SPI'.", "A web page's accessibility API is 'ARIA'."
embedding_text: accessibilityAPI: An accessibility API compatibility relation between a creative work and the accessibility API it supports. Also called API support, accessibility interface.

label: accessibilityControl
comment: Identifies input methods that are sufficient to fully control the described resource. Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessibilityControl-vocabulary).
enriched_comment: An accessibility control relation between a creative work and the input methods sufficient for its full control. Also called control methods, input compatibility, interaction modes. Examples: "A video game's accessibility control is 'keyboard'.", "A web application's accessibility control is 'mouse'."
embedding_text: accessibilityControl: An accessibility control relation between a creative work and the input methods sufficient for its full control. Also called control methods, input compatibility, interaction modes.

label: accessibilityFeature
comment: Content features of the resource, such as accessible media, alternatives and supported enhancements for accessibility. Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessibilityFeature-vocabulary).
enriched_comment: An accessibility feature relation between a creative work and its specific features designed to enhance accessibility. Also called accessible features, accessibility enhancements, content adaptations. Examples: "A movie's accessibility feature is 'captions'.", "An image's accessibility feature is 'altText'.", "A document's accessibility feature is 'highContrast'."
embedding_text: accessibilityFeature: An accessibility feature relation between a creative work and its specific features designed to enhance accessibility. Also called accessible features, accessibility enhancements, content adaptations.

label: accessibilityHazard
comment: A characteristic of the described resource that is physiologically dangerous to some users. Related to WCAG 2.0 guideline 2.3. Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessibilityHazard-vocabulary).
enriched_comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."
embedding_text: accessibilityHazard: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard.

label: accessibilitySummary
comment: A human-readable summary of specific accessibility features or deficiencies, consistent with the other accessibility metadata but expressing subtleties such as "short descriptions are present but long descriptions will be needed for non-visual users" or "short descriptions are present and no long descriptions are needed".
enriched_comment: An accessibility summary relation between a creative work and a human-readable text describing its accessibility features and deficiencies. Also called accessibility overview, access statement, accessibility report. Examples: "A website's accessibility summary states 'Short descriptions are present but long descriptions will be needed for non-visual users'.", "A document's accessibility summary notes 'Fully navigable by keyboard'."
embedding_text: accessibilitySummary: An accessibility summary relation between a creative work and a human-readable text describing its accessibility features and deficiencies. Also called accessibility overview, access statement, accessibility report.

label: accommodationCategory
comment: Category of an [[Accommodation]], following real estate conventions, e.g. RESO (see [PropertySubType](https://ddwiki.reso.org/display/DDW17/PropertySubType+Field), and [PropertyType](https://ddwiki.reso.org/display/DDW17/PropertyType+Field) fields for suggested values).
enriched_comment: An accommodation category relation between an accommodation and its classification type, often following real estate conventions. Also called property type, lodging category, dwelling classification. Examples: "A hotel room's accommodation category is 'Suite'.", "An apartment's accommodation category is 'Condo'.", "A house's accommodation category is 'SingleFamilyResidence'."
embedding_text: accommodationCategory: An accommodation category relation between an accommodation and its classification type, often following real estate conventions. Also called property type, lodging category, dwelling classification.

label: accommodationFloorPlan
comment: A floorplan of some [[Accommodation]].
enriched_comment: An accommodation floor plan relation between an accommodation or residence and its architectural layout. Also called layout diagram, property blueprint, room arrangement. Examples: "A hotel suite's accommodation floor plan shows two bedrooms.", "The residence's accommodation floor plan includes a garage."
embedding_text: accommodationFloorPlan: An accommodation floor plan relation between an accommodation or residence and its architectural layout. Also called layout diagram, property blueprint, room arrangement.

label: accountId
comment: The identifier for the account the payment will be applied to.
enriched_comment: An account identifier relation between an invoice and the text string identifying the account to which its payment will be applied. Also called billing account ID, customer account number, payment account reference. Examples: "An invoice's account ID is 'CUST12345'.", "The utility bill's account ID is '987654321'."
embedding_text: accountId: An account identifier relation between an invoice and the text string identifying the account to which its payment will be applied. Also called billing account ID, customer account number, payment account reference.

label: accountMinimumInflow
comment: A minimum amount that has to be paid in every month.
enriched_comment: An account minimum inflow relation between a bank account and the monetary amount that must be deposited monthly. Also called minimum monthly deposit, required inflow, minimum payment. Examples: "A savings account's minimum inflow is $50.", "The checking account's minimum inflow is €100."
embedding_text: accountMinimumInflow: An account minimum inflow relation between a bank account and the monetary amount that must be deposited monthly. Also called minimum monthly deposit, required inflow, minimum payment.

label: accountOverdraftLimit
comment: An overdraft is an extension of credit from a lending institution when an account reaches zero. An overdraft allows the individual to continue withdrawing money even if the account has no funds in it. Basically the bank allows people to borrow a set amount of money.
enriched_comment: An account overdraft limit relation between a bank account and the monetary amount representing the maximum credit extension allowed when funds are depleted. Also called overdraft maximum, credit limit, borrowing allowance. Examples: "A checking account's overdraft limit is $500.", "The business account's overdraft limit is £1000."
embedding_text: accountOverdraftLimit: An account overdraft limit relation between a bank account and the monetary amount representing the maximum credit extension allowed when funds are depleted. Also called overdraft maximum, credit limit, borrowing allowance.

label: accountablePerson
comment: Specifies the Person that is legally accountable for the CreativeWork.
enriched_comment: An accountable person relation between a creative work and the individual legally responsible for it. Also called legally responsible person, liable party, responsible individual. Examples: "A news article's accountable person is its editor-in-chief.", "A company report's accountable person is the CEO."
embedding_text: accountablePerson: An accountable person relation between a creative work and the individual legally responsible for it. Also called legally responsible person, liable party, responsible individual.

label: acquireLicensePage
comment: Indicates a page documenting how licenses can be purchased or otherwise acquired, for the current item.
enriched_comment: An acquire license page relation between a creative work and the web page or resource detailing how its licenses can be obtained. Also called licensing information page, purchase license URL, rights acquisition page. Examples: "A stock photo's acquire license page is its licensing terms URL.", "A software's acquire license page describes its purchase options."
embedding_text: acquireLicensePage: An acquire license page relation between a creative work and the web page or resource detailing how its licenses can be obtained. Also called licensing information page, purchase license URL, rights acquisition page.

label: acquiredFrom
comment: The organization or person from which the product was acquired.
enriched_comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."
embedding_text: acquiredFrom: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition.

label: acrissCode
comment: The ACRISS Car Classification Code is a code used by many car rental companies, for classifying vehicles. ACRISS stands for Association of Car Rental Industry Systems and Standards.
enriched_comment: An ACRISS code relation between a bus, coach, or car and its standardized classification code used by car rental companies. Also called car classification code, vehicle rental code. Examples: "A rental car's ACRISS code is 'ECAR'.", "A luxury sedan's ACRISS code is 'LDAR'."
embedding_text: acrissCode: An ACRISS code relation between a bus, coach, or car and its standardized classification code used by car rental companies. Also called car classification code, vehicle rental code.

label: actionAccessibilityRequirement
comment: A set of requirements that must be fulfilled in order to perform an Action. If more than one value is specified, fulfilling one set of requirements will allow the Action to be performed.
enriched_comment: An action accessibility requirement relation between a consume action and the specifications that must be met to perform it. Also called action prerequisites, access conditions, fulfillment requirements. Examples: "A 'watch movie' action's accessibility requirement is 'subscription'.", "A 'download software' action's accessibility requirement is 'login'."
embedding_text: actionAccessibilityRequirement: An action accessibility requirement relation between a consume action and the specifications that must be met to perform it. Also called action prerequisites, access conditions, fulfillment requirements.

label: actionApplication
comment: An application that can complete the request.
enriched_comment: An action application relation between an entry point and the software application capable of fulfilling the associated request. Also called handling application, processing app, execution software. Examples: "A 'send email' entry point's action application is 'Gmail'.", "A 'edit document' entry point's action application is 'Microsoft Word'." Distinct from application, which is a more general property for an application that can complete the request.
embedding_text: actionApplication: An action application relation between an entry point and the software application capable of fulfilling the associated request. Also called handling application, processing app, execution software.

label: actionOption
comment: A sub property of object. The options subject to this action.
enriched_comment: An action option relation between a choose action and the available choices or alternatives. Also called choice alternatives, selection options, available choices. Examples: "A 'choose color' action's action option is 'red'.", "A 'select size' action's action option is 'large'."
embedding_text: actionOption: An action option relation between a choose action and the available choices or alternatives. Also called choice alternatives, selection options, available choices.

label: actionPlatform
comment: The high level platform(s) where the Action can be performed for the given URL. To specify a specific application or operating system instance, use actionApplication.
enriched_comment: An action platform relation between an entry point and the high-level digital platform(s) where the associated action can be performed. Also called execution platform, supported environment, operating system. Examples: "A web application's action platform is 'WebPlatform'.", "A mobile app's action platform is 'iOS'."
embedding_text: actionPlatform: An action platform relation between an entry point and the high-level digital platform(s) where the associated action can be performed. Also called execution platform, supported environment, operating system.

label: actionProcess
comment: Description of the process by which the action was performed.
enriched_comment: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."
embedding_text: actionProcess: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide.

label: actionStatus
comment: Indicates the current disposition of the Action.
enriched_comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."
embedding_text: actionStatus: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition.

label: actionableFeedbackPolicy
comment: For a [[NewsMediaOrganization]] or other news-related [[Organization]], a statement about public engagement activities (for news media, the newsroom’s), including involving the public - digitally or otherwise -- in coverage decisions, reporting and activities after publication.
enriched_comment: An actionable feedback policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a creative work or URL detailing its public engagement and feedback mechanisms. Also called public engagement policy, feedback guidelines, reader interaction policy. Examples: "A news organization's actionable feedback policy is its 'Corrections and Feedback' page.", "The company's actionable feedback policy outlines how customers can submit suggestions."
embedding_text: actionableFeedbackPolicy: An actionable feedback policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a creative work or URL detailing its public engagement and feedback mechanisms. Also called public engagement policy, feedback guidelines, reader interaction policy.

label: activeIngredient
comment: An active ingredient, typically chemical compounds and/or biologic substances.
enriched_comment: An active ingredient relation between a dietary supplement, drug, drug strength, or substance and its primary chemical or biologic component. Also called main component, primary substance, key compound. Examples: "A pain reliever's active ingredient is 'ibuprofen'.", "A vitamin supplement's active ingredient is 'Vitamin C'."
embedding_text: activeIngredient: An active ingredient relation between a dietary supplement, drug, drug strength, or substance and its primary chemical or biologic component. Also called main component, primary substance, key compound.

label: activityDuration
comment: Length of time to engage in the activity.
enriched_comment: An activity duration relation between an exercise plan and the length of time recommended for engaging in the activity. Also called exercise length, workout time, session duration. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity duration is '30 minutes'.", "The yoga routine's activity duration is '1 hour'."
embedding_text: activityDuration: An activity duration relation between an exercise plan and the length of time recommended for engaging in the activity. Also called exercise length, workout time, session duration.

label: activityFrequency
comment: How often one should engage in the activity.
enriched_comment: An activity frequency relation between an exercise plan and how often the activity should be performed. Also called exercise frequency, workout schedule, repetition rate. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity frequency is '3 times per week'.", "The meditation guide's activity frequency is 'daily'."
embedding_text: activityFrequency: An activity frequency relation between an exercise plan and how often the activity should be performed. Also called exercise frequency, workout schedule, repetition rate.

label: actor
comment: An actor (individual or a group), e.g. in TV, radio, movie, video games etc., or in an event. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.
enriched_comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.
embedding_text: actor: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player.

label: actors
comment: An actor, e.g. in TV, radio, movie, video games etc. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.
enriched_comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.
embedding_text: actors: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player.

label: addOn
comment: An additional offer that can only be obtained in combination with the first base offer (e.g. supplements and extensions that are available for a surcharge).
enriched_comment: An add-on relation between a base offer and an additional offer that can only be acquired in conjunction with it. Also called supplementary offer, bundled offer, extra option. Examples: "A car purchase offer has an add-on for extended warranty.", "A software license offer has an add-on for premium support."
embedding_text: addOn: An add-on relation between a base offer and an additional offer that can only be acquired in conjunction with it. Also called supplementary offer, bundled offer, extra option.

label: additionalName
comment: An additional name for a Person, can be used for a middle name.
enriched_comment: An additional name relation between a person and a supplementary name, such as a middle name. Also called middle name, secondary name, other name. Examples: "A person's additional name is 'Marie'.", "John's additional name is 'Fitzgerald'."
embedding_text: additionalName: An additional name relation between a person and a supplementary name, such as a middle name. Also called middle name, secondary name, other name.

label: additionalNumberOfGuests
comment: If responding yes, the number of guests who will attend in addition to the invitee.
enriched_comment: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."
embedding_text: additionalNumberOfGuests: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees.

label: additionalProperty
comment: A property-value pair representing an additional characteristic of the entity, e.g. a product feature or another characteristic for which there is no matching property in schema.org.\n\nNote: Publishers should be aware that applications designed to use specific schema.org properties (e.g. https://schema.org/width, https://schema.org/color, https://schema.org/gtin13, ...) will typically expect such data to be provided using those properties, rather than using the generic property/value mechanism.
enriched_comment: An additional property relation between an entity (e.g., product, offer, place) and a property-value pair describing a characteristic not covered by specific schema.org properties. Also called extra characteristic, custom attribute, supplementary detail. Examples: "A product's additional property is 'waterResistance: IP68'.", "A place's additional property is 'historicalSignificance: high'."
embedding_text: additionalProperty: An additional property relation between an entity (e.g., product, offer, place) and a property-value pair describing a characteristic not covered by specific schema.org properties. Also called extra characteristic, custom attribute, supplementary detail.

label: additionalType
comment: An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org style guide .
enriched_comment: An additional type relation between a thing and a more specific type from an external vocabulary or a descriptive text. Also called supplementary type, extended type, semantic type. Examples: "A person's additional type is 'foaf:Agent'.", "A document's additional type is 'schema:Report'."
embedding_text: additionalType: An additional type relation between a thing and a more specific type from an external vocabulary or a descriptive text. Also called supplementary type, extended type, semantic type.

label: additionalVariable
comment: Any additional component of the exercise prescription that may need to be articulated to the patient. This may include the order of exercises, the number of repetitions of movement, quantitative distance, progressions over time, etc.
enriched_comment: An additional variable relation between an exercise plan and any extra components of the exercise prescription, such as exercise order or progression details. Also called exercise detail, workout parameter, prescription addendum. Examples: "An exercise plan's additional variable is 'Perform exercises in circuit order'.", "The rehabilitation plan's additional variable is 'Increase repetitions by 2 each week'."
embedding_text: additionalVariable: An additional variable relation between an exercise plan and any extra components of the exercise prescription, such as exercise order or progression details. Also called exercise detail, workout parameter, prescription addendum.

label: address
comment: Physical address of the item.
enriched_comment: An address relation between an entity (e.g., organization, person, place) and its physical postal address. Also called physical location, mailing address, street address. Examples: "A company's address is '123 Main St, Anytown'.", "A person's address is 'PO Box 123'.", "The restaurant's address is '456 Oak Ave'."
embedding_text: address: An address relation between an entity (e.g., organization, person, place) and its physical postal address. Also called physical location, mailing address, street address.

label: addressCountry
comment: The country. Recommended to be in 2-letter [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1) format, for example "US". For backward compatibility, a 3-letter [ISO 3166-1 alpha-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3) country code such as "SGP" or a full country name such as "Singapore" can also be used.
enriched_comment: An address country relation between a defined region, geo-coordinates, geo-shape, or postal address and the country it is located within. Also called nation, country code, geographic country. Examples: "A postal address's address country is 'US'.", "The coordinates' address country is 'France'."
embedding_text: addressCountry: An address country relation between a defined region, geo-coordinates, geo-shape, or postal address and the country it is located within. Also called nation, country code, geographic country.

label: addressLocality
comment: The locality in which the street address is, and which is in the region. For example, Mountain View.
enriched_comment: An address locality relation between a postal address and the city or town where it is situated. Also called city, town, municipality. Examples: "A postal address's address locality is 'Mountain View'.", "The address locality is 'London'."
embedding_text: addressLocality: An address locality relation between a postal address and the city or town where it is situated. Also called city, town, municipality.

label: addressRegion
comment: The region in which the locality is, and which is in the country. For example, California or another appropriate first-level [Administrative division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_administrative_divisions_by_country) such as the Province in Italy or Region in Germany.
enriched_comment: An address region relation between a defined region or postal address and the administrative division (e.g., state, province) it belongs to. Also called state, province, administrative area. Examples: "A postal address's address region is 'CA'.", "The address region is 'Bavaria'."
embedding_text: addressRegion: An address region relation between a defined region or postal address and the administrative division (e.g., state, province) it belongs to. Also called state, province, administrative area.

label: administrationRoute
comment: A route by which this drug may be administered, e.g. 'oral'.
enriched_comment: An administration route relation between a drug and the method by which it is intended to be given. Also called dosage route, delivery method, intake method. Examples: "A medication's administration route is 'oral'.", "An injection's administration route is 'intravenous'."
embedding_text: administrationRoute: An administration route relation between a drug and the method by which it is intended to be given. Also called dosage route, delivery method, intake method.

label: advanceBookingRequirement
comment: The amount of time that is required between accepting the offer and the actual usage of the resource or service.
enriched_comment: An advance booking requirement relation between a demand or offer and the minimum time needed between acceptance and actual usage. Also called lead time, booking lead time, reservation notice. Examples: "A flight offer's advance booking requirement is '24 hours'.", "The concert ticket demand has an advance booking requirement of '7 days'."
embedding_text: advanceBookingRequirement: An advance booking requirement relation between a demand or offer and the minimum time needed between acceptance and actual usage. Also called lead time, booking lead time, reservation notice.

label: adverseOutcome
comment: A possible complication and/or side effect of this therapy. label: artform

label: articleBody

label: asin
comment: An Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) is a 10-character alphanumeric unique identifier assigned by Amazon.com and its partners for product identification within the Amazon organization (summary from [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Standard_Identification_Number)'s article). Note also that this is a definition for how to include ASINs in Schema.org data, and not a definition of ASINs in general - see documentation from Amazon for authoritative details. ASINs are most commonly encoded as text strings, but the [asin] property supports URL/URI as potential values too.
enriched_comment: An Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) associated with a demand, offer, or product. Also called: Amazon product ID, ASIN identifier. Examples: "Product 'Book' asin 'B00005N53N'", "Offer 'Laptop' asin 'B07XXXXXXX'", "Demand 'Toy' asin 'B08YYYYYYY'."
embedding_text: asin: An Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) associated with a demand, offer, or product. Also called: Amazon product ID, ASIN identifier.

label: cutoffTime
comment: Order cutoff time allows merchants to describe the time after which they will no longer process orders received on that day. The time is indicated using the ISO-8601 Time format, e.g. "23:30:00-05:00" would represent 6:30 pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) which is 5 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

label: dateline
comment: A [dateline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dateline) is a brief piece of text included in news articles that describes where and when the story was written or filed though the date is often omitted. Sometimes only a placename is provided. Structured representations of dateline-related information can also be expressed more explicitly using [[locationCreated]] (which represents where a work was created, e.g. where a news report was written). For location depicted or described in the content, use [[contentLocation]]. Dateline summaries are oriented more towards human readers than towards automated processing, and can vary substantially. Some examples: "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Paris, France", "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington", "Beijing/Moscow", "QUEZON CITY, Philippines".
enriched_comment: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.
embedding_text: dateline: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location.

embedding_text: encodingFormat: An encoding format relation between a creative work or media object and the text or URL describing its media type. Also called "file format", "media type", "MIME type".

Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.
embedding_text: endDate: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date".

embedding_text: endOffset: An end offset relation between a clip and the number or HyperTocEntry representing its end time from the beginning of the work. Also called "clip end time", "segment end", "finish offset".

label: endTime
comment: The endTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to end. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. E.g. John wrote a book from January to *December*. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the end of a clip within a larger file.\n\nNote that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.
enriched_comment: An end time relation between an item (such as an action, reservation, or media object) and the time it is expected to conclude or when a clip ends. Also called "conclusion time", "finish time", "closing time". Examples: "Reservation 'Dinner' endTime '20:00'", "Action 'Meeting' endTime '17:00'", "Media clip endTime '00:02:30'". embedding_text: endTime: An end time relation between an item (such as an action, reservation, or media object) and the time it is expected to conclude or when a clip ends. Also called "conclusion time", "finish time", "closing time".

label: eventSchedule
comment: Associates an [[Event]] with a [[Schedule]]. There are circumstances where it is preferable to share a schedule for a series of repeating events rather than data on the individual events themselves. For example, a website or application might prefer to publish a schedule for a weekly gym class rather than provide data on every event. A schedule could be processed by applications to add forthcoming events to a calendar. An [[Event]] that is associated with a [[Schedule]] using this property should not have [[startDate]] or [[endDate]] properties. These are instead defined within the associated [[Schedule]], this avoids any ambiguity for clients using the data. The property might have repeated values to specify different schedules, e.g. for different months or seasons.

Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". * Note 3: Often, the absolute value is useful only when related to driving speed ("at 80 km/h") or usage pattern ("city traffic"). You can use [[valueReference]] to link the value for the fuel economy to another value.

label: geoContains
comment: Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a containing geometry to a contained geometry. enriched_comment: A geo contains relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place fully encloses another, with at least one interior point in common. Also called: encloses, encompasses, includes. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo contains "City 'Paris'", "Continent 'Europe'" geo contains "Country 'Germany'", "Building 'Empire State'" geo contains "Office 'Suite 100'". Distinct from geoWithin, which is the inverse relation.
embedding_text: geoContains: A geo contains relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place fully encloses another, with at least one interior point in common. Also called: encloses, encompasses, includes.

label: geoCoveredBy
comment: Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a geometry to another that covers it. As defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM).
enriched_comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.
embedding_text: geoCoveredBy: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by.

label: geoCovers
comment: Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a covering geometry to a covered geometry. "Every point of b is a point of (the interior or boundary of) a". As defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM).
enriched_comment: A geo covers relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place completely covers another, meaning every point of the covered entity is within the covering entity. Also called: covers, encompasses, overlies. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo covers "City 'Paris'", "North America" geo covers "Lake 'Superior'", "City 'Springfield'" geo covers "House '123 Main St'". Distinct from geoCoveredBy, which is the inverse relation.
embedding_text: geoCovers: A geo covers relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place completely covers another, meaning every point of the covered entity is within the covering entity. Also called: covers, encompasses, overlies.

embedding_text: geoCrosses: A geo crosses relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places intersect, sharing some but not all interior points, and their intersection has a lower dimension than at least one of them. Also called: intersects, traverses, cuts across.

embedding_text: globalLocationNumber: A global location number relation between an organization, person, or place and its unique 13-digit GLN identifier. Also called: GLN, International Location Number, ILN.

label: gtin
comment: A Global Trade Item Number ([GTIN](https://www.gs1.org/standards/id-keys/gtin)). GTINs identify trade items, including products and services, using numeric identification codes. A correct [[gtin]] value should be a valid GTIN, which means that it should be an all-numeric string of either 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits, or a "GS1 Digital Link" URL based on such a string. The numeric component should also have a [valid GS1 check digit](https://www.gs1.org/services/check-digit-calculator) and meet the other rules for valid GTINs. See also [GS1's GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) and [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Trade_Item_Number) for more details. Left-padding of the gtin values is not required or encouraged. The [[gtin]] property generalizes the earlier [[gtin8]], [[gtin12]], [[gtin13]], and [[gtin14]] properties. The GS1 [digital link specifications](https://www.gs1.org/standards/Digital-Link/) expresses GTINs as URLs (URIs, IRIs, etc.). Digital Links should be populated into the [[hasGS1DigitalLink]] attribute. Note also that this is a definition for how to include GTINs in Schema.org data, and not a definition of GTINs in general - see the GS1 documentation for authoritative details.
enriched_comment: A Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its unique numeric identification code. Also called: product identifier, trade item number, barcode number. Examples: "Product X" gtin "01234567890128", "Offer for Item Y" gtin "9876543210987", "Demand for Service Z" gtin "https://id.gs1.org/01/12345678901231". Distinct from gtin8, gtin12, gtin13, gtin14, which are more specific GTIN types.
embedding_text: gtin: A Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its unique numeric identification code. Also called: product identifier, trade item number, barcode number.

label: gtin12
comment: The GTIN-12 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. The GTIN-12 is the 12-digit GS1 Identification Key composed of a U.P.C. Company Prefix, Item Reference, and Check Digit used to identify trade items. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details.
enriched_comment: A GTIN-12 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 12-digit Global Trade Item Number. Also called: UPC code, GTIN-12 identifier, 12-digit barcode. Examples: "Grocery Item" gtin12 "012345678901", "Consumer Product" gtin12 "789012345678", "Retail Offer" gtin12 "000001111111". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.
embedding_text: gtin12: A GTIN-12 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 12-digit Global Trade Item Number. Also called: UPC code, GTIN-12 identifier, 12-digit barcode.

label: gtin13
comment: The GTIN-13 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This is equivalent to 13-digit ISBN codes and EAN UCC-13. Former 12-digit UPC codes can be converted into a GTIN-13 code by simply adding a preceding zero. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details.
enriched_comment: A GTIN-13 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 13-digit Global Trade Item Number, equivalent to EAN-13 or ISBN. Also called: EAN-13, ISBN-13, GTIN-13 identifier. Examples: "Book Product" gtin13 "9781234567890", "European Retail Item" gtin13 "5012345678901", "Offer for Book" gtin13 "9780123456789". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.
embedding_text: gtin13: A GTIN-13 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 13-digit Global Trade Item Number, equivalent to EAN-13 or ISBN. Also called: EAN-13, ISBN-13, GTIN-13 identifier.

label: gtin14
comment: The GTIN-14 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details.
enriched_comment: A GTIN-14 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 14-digit Global Trade Item Number, often used for trade items at different packaging levels. Also called: ITF-14, GTIN-14 identifier, shipping container code. Examples: "Case of Cans" gtin14 "10012345678905", "Pallet of Goods" gtin14 "00000012345678", "Wholesale Product" gtin14 "40123456789012". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.
embedding_text: gtin14: A GTIN-14 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 14-digit Global Trade Item Number, often used for trade items at different packaging levels. Also called: ITF-14, GTIN-14 identifier, shipping container code.

label: gtin8
comment: The GTIN-8 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This code is also known as EAN/UCC-8 or 8-digit EAN. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details.
enriched_comment: A GTIN-8 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 8-digit Global Trade Item Number, also known as EAN-8. Also called: EAN-8, GTIN-8 identifier, 8-digit barcode. Examples: "Small Retail Item" gtin8 "12345670", "Confectionery Product" gtin8 "98765432", "Offer for Small Product" gtin8 "00000001". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.
embedding_text: gtin8: A GTIN-8 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 8-digit Global Trade Item Number, also known as EAN-8. Also called: EAN-8, GTIN-8 identifier, 8-digit barcode.

label: guideline

enriched_comment: A guideline relation between a medical entity and a related medical guideline. Also called: related guideline, medical recommendation, clinical protocol. Examples: "Hypertension" guideline "AHA Guideline for Hypertension", "Diabetes Treatment" guideline "NICE Guideline for Diabetes", "COVID-19 Management" guideline "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines". embedding_text: guideline: A guideline relation between a medical entity and a related medical guideline. Also called: related guideline, medical recommendation, clinical protocol.

embedding_text: guidelineDate: A guideline date relation between a medical guideline and the date its recommendations were issued. Also called: recommendation date, issue date, publication date.

label: guidelineSubject

embedding_text: guidelineSubject: A guideline subject relation between a medical guideline and the medical conditions, treatments, or other entities it addresses. Also called: guideline topic, subject matter, focus.

label: handlingTime
comment: The typical delay between the receipt of the order and the goods either leaving the warehouse or being prepared for pickup, in case the delivery method is on site pickup. In the context of [[ShippingDeliveryTime]], Typical properties: minValue, maxValue, unitCode (d for DAY). This is by common convention assumed to mean business days (if a unitCode is used, coded as "d"), i.e. only counting days when the business normally operates. In the context of [[ShippingService]], use the [[ServicePeriod]] format, that contains the same information in a structured form, with cut-off time, business days and duration.
enriched_comment: A processing time relation between a shipping service or delivery time and the duration required for order fulfillment. Also called processing duration, preparation time, fulfillment time, lead time. Examples: "A shipping service has a handling time of 2 days.", "The delivery time includes a handling time of 1-3 business days.", "Order processing has a handling time of 24 hours."
embedding_text: handlingTime: A processing time relation between a shipping service or delivery time and the duration required for order fulfillment. Also called processing duration, preparation time, fulfillment time, lead time.

embedding_text: hasAdultConsideration: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only.

embedding_text: hasBioChemEntityPart: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of.

embedding_text: hasBioPolymerSequence: A sequence representation relation between a gene or protein and its symbolic biopolymer sequence. Also called sequence is, contains sequence, biopolymer sequence of.

enriched_comment: A course inclusion relation between an educational or occupational program and one of its constituent courses. Also called includes course, program course, course part of. embedding_text: hasCourse: A course inclusion relation between an educational or occupational program and one of its constituent courses. Also called includes course, program course, course part of.

enriched_comment: A course offering relation between a course and a specific instance of that course. Also called course offering, instance of course, course session. embedding_text: hasCourseInstance: A course offering relation between a course and a specific instance of that course. Also called course offering, instance of course, course session.

embedding_text: hasCredential: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential.

embedding_text: hasDefinedTerm: A term inclusion relation between a defined term set or taxon and one of its contained defined terms. Also called contains term, includes term, term within.

embedding_text: hasDeliveryMethod: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery.

embedding_text: hasDigitalDocumentPermission: A document permission relation between a digital document and an associated access permission. Also called document access, permission for document, document rights.

label: hasDriveThroughService

Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."
embedding_text: hasDriveThroughService: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service.

label: hasEnergyConsumptionDetails

enriched_comment: An energy consumption detail relation between a product and its energy efficiency information. Also called energy efficiency details, energy rating details, consumption specifics. Examples: "A refrigerator has energy consumption details.", "An appliance has energy consumption details for its class.", "The product's energy consumption details are listed."
embedding_text: hasEnergyConsumptionDetails: An energy consumption detail relation between a product and its energy efficiency information. Also called energy efficiency details, energy rating details, consumption specifics.

label: hasEnergyEfficiencyCategory
comment: Defines the energy efficiency Category (which could be either a rating out of range of values or a yes/no certification) for a product according to an international energy efficiency standard.
enriched_comment: An energy efficiency category relation between energy consumption details and an energy efficiency rating. Also called energy class, efficiency rating, energy grade. Examples: "Energy consumption details have an energy efficiency category of A+++.", "The details show an energy efficiency category of 'certified'.", "This product's details indicate an energy efficiency category.". Distinct from hasEnergyConsumptionDetails, which describes the full set of energy consumption information.
embedding_text: hasEnergyEfficiencyCategory: An energy efficiency category relation between energy consumption details and an energy efficiency rating. Also called energy class, efficiency rating, energy grade.

label: hasGS1DigitalLink
comment: The GS1 digital link associated with the object. This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products: A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI 21 ) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]] A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI 10 ) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product. A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI 8013 ) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]]. Other item types should be adapted similarly.
enriched_comment: A GS1 digital link relation between an offer, organization, place, or product and its associated GS1 digital link URL. Also called GS1 link, digital link, product link. Examples: "A product has a GS1 digital link for traceability.", "An organization has a GS1 digital link for its profile.", "The offer includes a GS1 digital link."
embedding_text: hasGS1DigitalLink: A GS1 digital link relation between an offer, organization, place, or product and its associated GS1 digital link URL. Also called GS1 link, digital link, product link.

label: hasHealthAspect
comment: Indicates the aspect or aspects specifically addressed in some [[HealthTopicContent]]. For example, that the content is an overview, or that it talks about treatment, self-care, treatments or their side-effects.
enriched_comment: A health aspect relation between health topic content and the specific health aspect it addresses. Also called content aspect, topic aspect, health focus. Examples: "Health topic content has a health aspect of 'treatment'.", "The article has a health aspect of 'self-care'.", "This content addresses a health aspect of 'overview'."
embedding_text: hasHealthAspect: A health aspect relation between health topic content and the specific health aspect it addresses. Also called content aspect, topic aspect, health focus.

label: hasMap

embedding_text: hasMap: A map relation between a place and its associated map or map URL. Also called map of, location map, geographical map.

label: hasMeasurement

enriched_comment: A measurement relation between a certification, offer, product, or size specification and a quantitative value representing a specific measurement. Also called item measurement, dimension, size value. Examples: "A product has a measurement for its height.", "An offer includes a measurement for package weight.", "The certification has a measurement of carbon footprint."
embedding_text: hasMeasurement: A measurement relation between a certification, offer, product, or size specification and a quantitative value representing a specific measurement. Also called item measurement, dimension, size value.

label: hasMemberProgram

embedding_text: hasMemberProgram: A member program relation between an organization and a member program it offers. Also called offers program, loyalty program, membership program.

label: hasMenu

embedding_text: hasMenu: A menu relation between a food establishment and its menu (structured, text, or URL). Also called offers menu, menu available, food menu.

embedding_text: hasMenuItem: A menu item inclusion relation between a menu or menu section and one of its contained menu items. Also called includes item, menu item of, item on menu.

embedding_text: hasMenuSection: A menu section inclusion relation between a menu or menu section and one of its contained menu sections. Also called includes section, menu subgroup, section of menu.

label: hasMerchantReturnPolicy

embedding_text: hasMerchantReturnPolicy: A merchant return policy relation between an offer, organization, or product and its applicable return policy. Also called return policy, refund policy, returns information.

label: hasMolecularFunction

enriched_comment: A molecular function relation between a biochemical entity and its performed molecular function. Also called performs function, molecular role, functional activity. Examples: "A protein has a molecular function of enzyme activity.", "This BioChemEntity has a molecular function described by a defined term.", "The entity's molecular function is specified."
embedding_text: hasMolecularFunction: A molecular function relation between a biochemical entity and its performed molecular function. Also called performs function, molecular role, functional activity.

label: hasOccupation

enriched_comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."
embedding_text: hasOccupation: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment.

label: hasOfferCatalog
comment: Indicates an OfferCatalog listing for this Organization, Person, or Service.
enriched_comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."
embedding_text: hasOfferCatalog: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog.

label: hasPOS

Examples: "An organization has a POS in New York.", "The vendor has a POS at the market.", "This company operates multiple POS locations."
embedding_text: hasPOS: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point.

label: hasPart
comment: Indicates an item or CreativeWork that is part of this item, or CreativeWork (in some sense).

embedding_text: hasPart: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of.

label: hasParticipationOffer

label: incentiveAmount
comment: Describes the amount that can be redeemed from this incentive. [[QuantitativeValue]]: Use this for incentives based on price (either raw amount or percentage-based). For a raw amount example, "You can claim $2,500 - $7,500 from the total cost of installation" would be represented as the following: { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", “minValue”: 2500, “maxValue”: 7500, "unitCode": "USD" } [[QuantitativeValue]] can also be used for percentage amounts. In such cases, value is used to represent the incentive’s percentage, while maxValue represents a limit (if one exists) to that incentive. The unitCode should be 'P1' and the unitText should be '%', while valueReference should be used for holding the currency type. For example, "You can claim up to 30% of the total cost of installation, up to a maximum of $7,500" would be: { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "value": 30, "unitCode": "P1", "unitText": "%", “maxValue”: 7500, “valueReference”: “USD” } [[UnitPriceSpecification]]: Use this for incentives that are based on amounts rather than price. For example, a net metering rebate that pays $10/kWh, up to $1,000: { "@type": "UnitPriceSpecification", "price": 10, "priceCurrency": "USD", "referenceQuantity": 1, "unitCode": "DO3", "unitText": "kw/h", "maxPrice": 1000, "description": "$10 / kwh up to $1000" } [[LoanOrCredit]]: Use for incentives that are loan based. For example, a loan of $4,000 - $50,000 with a repayment term of 10 years, interest free would look like: { "@type": "LoanOrCredit", "loanTerm": { "@type":"QuantitativeValue", "value":"10", "unitCode": "ANN" }, "amount":[ { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "Name":"fixed interest rate", "value":"0", }, ], "amount":[ { "@type": "MonetaryAmount", "Name":"min loan amount", "value":"4000", "currency":"CAD" }, { "@type": "MonetaryAmount", "Name":"max loan amount", "value":"50000", "currency":"CAD" } ], } In summary: Use [[QuantitativeValue]] for absolute/percentage-based incentives applied on the price of a good/service. Use [[UnitPriceSpecification]] for incentives based on a per-unit basis (e.g. net metering). Use [[LoanOrCredit]] for loans/credits. .

label: iso6523Code
comment: An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The identifier should be in the `XXXX:YYYYYY:ZZZ` or `XXXX:YYYYYY`format. Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous.
enriched_comment: An organization identification relation between an organization and its globally standardized ISO 6523 code. Also called ISO 6523 identifier, organization code, international organization ID. Examples: An organization has an iso6523Code of '0060:802000000'. A company has an iso6523Code of '0199:LEI1234567890'. A business has an iso6523Code of '0088:1234567890123'. Distinct from leiCode, duns, globalLocationNumber, vatID, or taxID, as this is a more general, structured international identifier that can encompass those.
embedding_text: iso6523Code: An organization identification relation between an organization and its globally standardized ISO 6523 code. Also called ISO 6523 identifier, organization code, international organization ID.

label: itemListElement
comment:
For itemListElement values, you can use simple strings (e.g. "Peter", "Paul", "Mary"), existing entities, or use ListItem.

Text values are best if the elements in the list are plain strings. Existing entities are best for a simple, unordered list of existing things in your data. ListItem is used with ordered lists when you want to provide additional context about the element in that list or when the same item might be in different places in different lists.

Note: The order of elements in your mark-up is not sufficient for indicating the order or elements. Use ListItem with a 'position' property in such cases.

An item list has itemListElement a ListItem for 'Task 1'. Distinct from item, which refers to the entity *within* a ListItem, not the ListItem itself or a direct string/entity in the list.

label: lowPrice
comment:
The lowest price of all offers available.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.

label: maintainer
comment: A maintainer of a [[Dataset]], software package ([[SoftwareApplication]]), or other [[Project]]. A maintainer is a [[Person]] or [[Organization]] that manages contributions to, and/or publication of, some (typically complex) artifact. It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.

Also called: project manager, curator, responsible party. Examples: "Software Package maintainer John Doe", "Dataset maintainer Open Data Initiative", "Website maintainer Webmaster Team".

The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. In most cases, it would be pointless and counter productive to attempt to update all [[url]] markup to use [[mobileUrl]] for more mobile-oriented pages.
