label: naics
comment: The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for a particular organization or business person.
enriched_comment: A North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with an organization or business person. Also called NAICS code, industry classification code, business classification code. Examples: "Company A naics '511210' (Software Publishers)", "Person B naics '541611' (Administrative Management and General Management Services)", "Restaurant C naics '722511' (Full-Service Restaurants)". Distinct from isicV4, which is the International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities.
embedding_text: naics: A North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with an organization or business person. Also called NAICS code, industry classification code, business classification code.

label: name
comment: The name of the item.
enriched_comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.
embedding_text: name: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label.

label: namedPosition
comment: A position played, performed or filled by a person or organization, as part of an organization. For example, an athlete in a SportsTeam might play in the position named 'Quarterback'.
enriched_comment: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title. Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of a role.
embedding_text: namedPosition: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title.

label: nationality
comment: Nationality of the person.
enriched_comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.
embedding_text: nationality: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity.

label: naturalProgression
comment: The expected progression of the condition if it is not treated and allowed to progress naturally.
enriched_comment: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition. Examples: "Common Cold naturalProgression 'resolves in 7-10 days'", "Untreated Diabetes naturalProgression 'leads to complications like neuropathy and kidney failure'", "Flu naturalProgression 'fever and body aches for 3-5 days, then recovery'". Distinct from prognosis, which is a forecast of the likely course of a disease.
embedding_text: naturalProgression: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition.

label: negativeNotes
comment: Provides negative considerations regarding something, most typically in pro/con lists for reviews (alongside [[positiveNotes]]). For symmetry In the case of a [[Review]], the property describes the [[itemReviewed]] from the perspective of the review; in the case of a [[Product]], the product itself is being described. Since product descriptions tend to emphasise positive claims, it may be relatively unusual to find [[negativeNotes]] used in this way. Nevertheless for the sake of symmetry, [[negativeNotes]] can be used on [[Product]]. The property values can be expressed either as unstructured text (repeated as necessary), or if ordered, as a list (in which case the most negative is at the beginning of the list).
enriched_comment: Negative considerations or drawbacks associated with a product or described in a review. Also called cons, disadvantages, downsides, criticisms. Examples: "Product X negativeNotes 'short battery life'", "Review Y negativeNotes 'poor customer service'", "Software Z negativeNotes 'steep learning curve', 'frequent crashes'". Distinct from positiveNotes, which describes favorable aspects.
embedding_text: negativeNotes: Negative considerations or drawbacks associated with a product or described in a review. Also called cons, disadvantages, downsides, criticisms.

label: nerve
comment: The underlying innervation associated with the muscle.
enriched_comment: A nerve providing innervation to a muscle. Also called innervated by, muscle innervation, nerve supply. Examples: "Biceps Brachii nerve 'Musculocutaneous nerve'", "Triceps Brachii nerve 'Radial nerve'", "Diaphragm nerve 'Phrenic nerve'". Distinct from nerveMotor, which describes the muscle controlled by a nerve.
embedding_text: nerve: A nerve providing innervation to a muscle. Also called innervated by, muscle innervation, nerve supply.

label: nerveMotor
comment: The neurological pathway extension that involves muscle control.
enriched_comment: A muscle controlled by a nerve through a neurological pathway. Also called motor innervation, controls muscle, innervates muscle. Examples: "Radial Nerve nerveMotor 'Triceps Brachii'", "Musculocutaneous Nerve nerveMotor 'Biceps Brachii'", "Phrenic Nerve nerveMotor 'Diaphragm'". Distinct from nerve, which describes the nerve of a muscle.
embedding_text: nerveMotor: A muscle controlled by a nerve through a neurological pathway. Also called motor innervation, controls muscle, innervates muscle.

label: netWorth
comment: The total financial value of the person as calculated by subtracting the total value of liabilities from the total value of assets.
enriched_comment: The total financial value of a person, calculated as assets minus liabilities. Also called personal wealth, financial worth, total assets. Examples: "Person A netWorth '$1,000,000'", "Person B netWorth '$500,000'", "Person C netWorth '$10,000'".
embedding_text: netWorth: The total financial value of a person, calculated as assets minus liabilities. Also called personal wealth, financial worth, total assets.

label: newsUpdatesAndGuidelines
comment: Indicates a page with news updates and guidelines. This could often be (but is not required to be) the main page containing [[SpecialAnnouncement]] markup on a site.
enriched_comment: A URL or web content providing news updates and guidelines related to a special announcement. Also called updates page, guidelines link, news and guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://example.com/covid-updates'", "Emergency Alert newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://gov.example.org/emergency-guidelines'", "Product Recall newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://company.com/recall-info'".
embedding_text: newsUpdatesAndGuidelines: A URL or web content providing news updates and guidelines related to a special announcement. Also called updates page, guidelines link, news and guidance.

label: nextItem
comment: A link to the ListItem that follows the current one.
enriched_comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.
embedding_text: nextItem: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list.

label: noBylinesPolicy
comment: For a [[NewsMediaOrganization]] or other news-related [[Organization]], a statement explaining when authors of articles are not named in bylines.
enriched_comment: A policy statement from a news media organization explaining when authors are not credited in bylines. Also called anonymous author policy, byline exclusion policy, uncredited author policy. Examples: "News Org A noBylinesPolicy 'https://news.example.com/bylines'", "Journalism Company B noBylinesPolicy 'Our policy is to omit bylines for staff editorials.'", "Media Outlet C noBylinesPolicy 'https://media.example.org/editorial-standards#bylines'".
embedding_text: noBylinesPolicy: A policy statement from a news media organization explaining when authors are not credited in bylines. Also called anonymous author policy, byline exclusion policy, uncredited author policy.

label: nonEqual
comment: This ordering relation for qualitative values indicates that the subject is not equal to the object.
enriched_comment: A qualitative value that is not equal to another qualitative value. Also called not equivalent to, different from, unequal to. Examples: "Value A nonEqual 'Value B'", "Color Red nonEqual 'Color Blue'", "Size Small nonEqual 'Size Large'". Distinct from equal, which indicates equivalence.
embedding_text: nonEqual: A qualitative value that is not equal to another qualitative value. Also called not equivalent to, different from, unequal to.

label: nonProprietaryName
comment: The generic name of this drug or supplement.
enriched_comment: The generic or non-proprietary name of a drug or dietary supplement. Also called generic name, common name, chemical name. Examples: "Drug X nonProprietaryName 'Acetaminophen'", "Supplement Y nonProprietaryName 'Ascorbic Acid'", "Medication Z nonProprietaryName 'Ibuprofen'". Distinct from proprietaryName, which is the brand or trade name.
embedding_text: nonProprietaryName: The generic or non-proprietary name of a drug or dietary supplement. Also called generic name, common name, chemical name.

label: nonprofitStatus
comment: nonprofitStatus indicates the legal status of a non-profit organization in its primary place of business.
enriched_comment: The legal nonprofit status of an organization in its primary place of business. Also called charitable status, tax-exempt status, non-profit classification. Examples: "Charity A nonprofitStatus 'Nonprofit501c3'", "Foundation B nonprofitStatus 'NonprofitType.Nonprofit501c4'", "Association C nonprofitStatus 'NonprofitType.Nonprofit501c6'".
embedding_text: nonprofitStatus: The legal nonprofit status of an organization in its primary place of business. Also called charitable status, tax-exempt status, non-profit classification.

label: normalRange
comment: Range of acceptable values for a typical patient, when applicable.
enriched_comment: The range of acceptable values for a medical test in a typical patient. Also called reference range, healthy range, typical values. Examples: "Blood Pressure Test normalRange '120/80 mmHg'", "Glucose Test normalRange '70-99 mg/dL'", "Cholesterol Test normalRange 'Total <200 mg/dL'".
embedding_text: normalRange: The range of acceptable values for a medical test in a typical patient. Also called reference range, healthy range, typical values.

label: nsn
comment: Indicates the [NATO stock number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO_Stock_Number) (nsn) of a [[Product]].
enriched_comment: A NATO Stock Number (NSN) identifying a product. Also called NATO stock number, military stock number, supply classification number. Examples: "Military Radio nsn '5820-01-123-4567'", "Vehicle Part nsn '2510-00-987-6543'", "Medical Kit nsn '6545-01-000-1111'". Distinct from gtin, which is a commercial global trade item number.
embedding_text: nsn: A NATO Stock Number (NSN) identifying a product. Also called NATO stock number, military stock number, supply classification number.

label: numAdults
comment: The number of adults staying in the unit.
enriched_comment: The number of adults included in a lodging reservation. Also called adult count, number of grown-ups, adult guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numAdults 2", "Vacation Rental numAdults 4", "Single Room Reservation numAdults 1". Distinct from numChildren, which specifies the number of children.
embedding_text: numAdults: The number of adults included in a lodging reservation. Also called adult count, number of grown-ups, adult guests.

label: numChildren
comment: The number of children staying in the unit.
enriched_comment: The number of children included in a lodging reservation. Also called child count, number of kids, child guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numChildren 1", "Vacation Rental numChildren 3", "Family Suite Reservation numChildren 2". Distinct from numAdults, which specifies the number of adults.
embedding_text: numChildren: The number of children included in a lodging reservation. Also called child count, number of kids, child guests.

label: numConstraints
comment: Indicates the number of constraints property values defined for a particular [[ConstraintNode]] such as [[StatisticalVariable]]. This helps applications understand if they have access to a sufficiently complete description of a [[StatisticalVariable]] or other construct that is defined using properties on template-style nodes.
enriched_comment: The number of constraint property values defined for a constraint node. Also called constraint count, number of restrictions, defined constraints. Examples: "Statistical Variable A numConstraints 3", "Data Filter B numConstraints 2", "Query Parameter C numConstraints 1".
embedding_text: numConstraints: The number of constraint property values defined for a constraint node. Also called constraint count, number of restrictions, defined constraints.

label: numItems
comment: Limits the number of items being shipped for which these conditions apply.
enriched_comment: A limit on the number of items being shipped for which specific shipping conditions apply. Also called item quantity limit, shipping item count, maximum items. Examples: "Free Shipping Conditions numItems 'max 5'", "Bulk Discount Shipping numItems 'min 10'", "Special Rate Shipping numItems '1-3'". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.
embedding_text: numItems: A limit on the number of items being shipped for which specific shipping conditions apply. Also called item quantity limit, shipping item count, maximum items.

label: numTracks
comment: The number of tracks in this album or playlist.
enriched_comment: The total number of tracks contained within a music playlist or album. Also called track count, song count, number of songs. Examples: "Album X numTracks 12", "Playlist Y numTracks 50", "EP Z numTracks 4". Distinct from numberOfEpisodes, which is for seasons or series.
embedding_text: numTracks: The total number of tracks contained within a music playlist or album. Also called track count, song count, number of songs.

label: numberOfAccommodationUnits
comment: Indicates the total (available plus unavailable) number of accommodation units in an [[ApartmentComplex]], or the number of accommodation units for a specific [[FloorPlan]] (within its specific [[ApartmentComplex]]). See also [[numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits]].
enriched_comment: The total number of accommodation units in an apartment complex or for a specific floor plan. Also called total units, unit count, accommodation unit total. Examples: "Apartment Complex A numberOfAccommodationUnits 150", "Floor Plan B numberOfAccommodationUnits 10", "Building C numberOfAccommodationUnits 200". Distinct from numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits, which specifies only the currently available units.
embedding_text: numberOfAccommodationUnits: The total number of accommodation units in an apartment complex or for a specific floor plan. Also called total units, unit count, accommodation unit total.

label: numberOfAirbags
comment: The number or type of airbags in the vehicle.
enriched_comment: The number or type of airbags present in a vehicle. Also called airbag count, vehicle airbags, safety airbags. Examples: "Car X numberOfAirbags 6", "SUV Y numberOfAirbags '8 (front, side, curtain)'", "Truck Z numberOfAirbags 2".
embedding_text: numberOfAirbags: The number or type of airbags present in a vehicle. Also called airbag count, vehicle airbags, safety airbags.

label: numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits
comment: Indicates the number of available accommodation units in an [[ApartmentComplex]], or the number of accommodation units for a specific [[FloorPlan]] (within its specific [[ApartmentComplex]]). See also [[numberOfAccommodationUnits]].
enriched_comment: The number of currently available accommodation units in an apartment complex or for a specific floor plan. Also called available units, vacant units, units for rent. Examples: "Apartment Complex A numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits 10", "Floor Plan B numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits 2", "Building C numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits 15". Distinct from numberOfAccommodationUnits, which specifies the total (available + unavailable) units.
embedding_text: numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits: The number of currently available accommodation units in an apartment complex or for a specific floor plan. Also called available units, vacant units, units for rent.

label: numberOfAxles
comment: The number of axles.\n\nTypical unit code(s): C62.
enriched_comment: The number of axles on a vehicle. Also called axle count, vehicle axles, axles quantity. Examples: "Car X numberOfAxles 2", "Truck Y numberOfAxles 3", "Trailer Z numberOfAxles 4".
embedding_text: numberOfAxles: The number of axles on a vehicle. Also called axle count, vehicle axles, axles quantity.

label: numberOfBathroomsTotal
comment: The total integer number of bathrooms in some [[Accommodation]], following real estate conventions as [documented in RESO](https://ddwiki.reso.org/display/DDW17/BathroomsTotalInteger+Field): "The simple sum of the number of bathrooms. For example for a property with two Full Bathrooms and one Half Bathroom, the Bathrooms Total Integer will be 3.". See also [[numberOfRooms]].
enriched_comment: The total integer count of all bathrooms (full, three-quarter, and half) within an accommodation or floor plan. Also called total bathroom count, bathroom total, sum of bathrooms. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfBathroomsTotal 2", "House B numberOfBathroomsTotal 3", "Hotel Room C numberOfBathroomsTotal 1". Distinct from numberOfFullBathrooms and numberOfPartialBathrooms, which specify specific types of bathrooms.
embedding_text: numberOfBathroomsTotal: The total integer count of all bathrooms (full, three-quarter, and half) within an accommodation or floor plan. Also called total bathroom count, bathroom total, sum of bathrooms.

label: numberOfBedrooms
comment: The total integer number of bedrooms in a some [[Accommodation]], [[ApartmentComplex]] or [[FloorPlan]].
enriched_comment: The total number of bedrooms in an accommodation, apartment complex, or floor plan. Also called bedroom count, number of sleeping rooms, bedroom total. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfBedrooms 2", "House B numberOfBedrooms 4", "Floor Plan C numberOfBedrooms 3". Distinct from numberOfBeds, which specifies the quantity of individual beds.
embedding_text: numberOfBedrooms: The total number of bedrooms in an accommodation, apartment complex, or floor plan. Also called bedroom count, number of sleeping rooms, bedroom total.

label: numberOfBeds
comment: The quantity of the given bed type available in the HotelRoom, Suite, House, or Apartment.
enriched_comment: The quantity of a specific bed type available within a lodging unit. Also called bed count, quantity of beds, available beds. Examples: "King Bed Details numberOfBeds 1", "Twin Bed Details numberOfBeds 2", "Queen Bed Details numberOfBeds 1". Distinct from numberOfBedrooms, which specifies the number of rooms designated as bedrooms.
embedding_text: numberOfBeds: The quantity of a specific bed type available within a lodging unit. Also called bed count, quantity of beds, available beds.

label: numberOfCredits
comment: The number of credits or units awarded by a Course or required to complete an EducationalOccupationalProgram.
enriched_comment: The number of credits or units awarded by a course or required for an educational occupational program. Also called credit hours, course units, program credits. Examples: "Calculus I Course numberOfCredits 3", "MBA Program numberOfCredits 60", "Certification Program numberOfCredits 10".
embedding_text: numberOfCredits: The number of credits or units awarded by a course or required for an educational occupational program. Also called credit hours, course units, program credits.

label: numberOfDoors
comment: The number of doors.\n\nTypical unit code(s): C62.
enriched_comment: The number of doors on a vehicle. Also called door count, vehicle doors, doors quantity. Examples: "Sedan X numberOfDoors 4", "Coupe Y numberOfDoors 2", "Hatchback Z numberOfDoors 5".
embedding_text: numberOfDoors: The number of doors on a vehicle. Also called door count, vehicle doors, doors quantity.

label: numberOfEmployees
comment: The number of employees in an organization, e.g. business.
enriched_comment: The number of employees working for an organization or targeted by a business audience. Also called employee count, workforce size, staff number. Examples: "Company A numberOfEmployees 500", "Small Business B numberOfEmployees 15", "Target Audience C numberOfEmployees '100-500'".
embedding_text: numberOfEmployees: The number of employees working for an organization or targeted by a business audience. Also called employee count, workforce size, staff number.

label: numberOfEpisodes
comment: The number of episodes in this season or series.
enriched_comment: The total number of episodes within a creative work season, radio series, TV series, or video game series. Also called episode count, series episodes, season episodes. Examples: "TV Series X numberOfEpisodes 200", "Season 1 numberOfEpisodes 10", "Video Game Series Y numberOfEpisodes 5". Distinct from numTracks, which is for music.
embedding_text: numberOfEpisodes: The total number of episodes within a creative work season, radio series, TV series, or video game series. Also called episode count, series episodes, season episodes.

label: numberOfForwardGears
comment: The total number of forward gears available for the transmission system of the vehicle.\n\nTypical unit code(s): C62.
enriched_comment: The total number of forward gears available in a vehicle's transmission system. Also called forward gear count, transmission gears, gear ratio count. Examples: "Car X numberOfForwardGears 6", "Truck Y numberOfForwardGears 8", "Motorcycle Z numberOfForwardGears 5".
embedding_text: numberOfForwardGears: The total number of forward gears available in a vehicle's transmission system. Also called forward gear count, transmission gears, gear ratio count.

label: numberOfFullBathrooms
comment: Number of full bathrooms - The total number of full and ¾ bathrooms in an [[Accommodation]]. This corresponds to the [BathroomsFull field in RESO](https://ddwiki.reso.org/display/DDW17/BathroomsFull+Field).
enriched_comment: The total number of full and three-quarter bathrooms in an accommodation or floor plan. Also called full bathroom count, full baths, complete bathrooms. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfFullBathrooms 2", "House B numberOfFullBathrooms 3", "Hotel Room C numberOfFullBathrooms 1". Distinct from numberOfPartialBathrooms, which specifies half or quarter bathrooms. numberOfBathroomsTotal is the sum of all types.
embedding_text: numberOfFullBathrooms: The total number of full and three-quarter bathrooms in an accommodation or floor plan. Also called full bathroom count, full baths, complete bathrooms.

label: numberOfItems
comment: The number of items in an ItemList. Note that some descriptions might not fully describe all items in a list (e.g., multi-page pagination); in such cases, the numberOfItems would be for the entire list.
enriched_comment: The total number of items contained within an item list. Also called item count, list size, total items. Examples: "Shopping Cart ItemList numberOfItems 5", "To-Do List numberOfItems 10", "Search Results List numberOfItems 100". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on items for shipping.
embedding_text: numberOfItems: The total number of items contained within an item list. Also called item count, list size, total items.

label: numberOfLoanPayments
comment: The number of payments contractually required at origination to repay the loan. For monthly paying loans this is the number of months from the contractual first payment date to the maturity date.
enriched_comment: The total number of payments contractually required to repay a loan. Also called loan payment count, repayment installments, number of installments. Examples: "Mortgage Repayment numberOfLoanPayments 360", "Car Loan Repayment numberOfLoanPayments 60", "Personal Loan Repayment numberOfLoanPayments 24".
embedding_text: numberOfLoanPayments: The total number of payments contractually required to repay a loan. Also called loan payment count, repayment installments, number of installments.

label: numberOfPages
comment: The number of pages in the book.
enriched_comment: The total number of pages in a book. Also called page count, book length, total pages. Examples: "Novel X numberOfPages 350", "Textbook Y numberOfPages 800", "Children's Book Z numberOfPages 32". Distinct from pagination, which describes page ranges.
embedding_text: numberOfPages: The total number of pages in a book. Also called page count, book length, total pages.

label: numberOfPartialBathrooms
comment: Number of partial bathrooms - The total number of half and ¼ bathrooms in an [[Accommodation]]. This corresponds to the [BathroomsPartial field in RESO](https://ddwiki.reso.org/display/DDW17/BathroomsPartial+Field).
enriched_comment: The total number of half and quarter bathrooms in an accommodation or floor plan. Also called partial bathroom count, half baths, quarter baths. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfPartialBathrooms 1", "House B numberOfPartialBathrooms 2", "Hotel Room C numberOfPartialBathrooms 0". Distinct from numberOfFullBathrooms, which specifies full or three-quarter bathrooms. numberOfBathroomsTotal is the sum of all types.
embedding_text: numberOfPartialBathrooms: The total number of half and quarter bathrooms in an accommodation or floor plan. Also called partial bathroom count, half baths, quarter baths.

label: numberOfPlayers
comment: Indicate how many people can play this game (minimum, maximum, or range).
enriched_comment: The number of people who can play a game or video game series, often expressed as a minimum, maximum, or range. Also called player count, game capacity, participant number. Examples: "Board Game X numberOfPlayers '2-4'", "Video Game Y numberOfPlayers '1 (single-player)'", "Online Game Z numberOfPlayers '100 (max)'".
embedding_text: numberOfPlayers: The number of people who can play a game or video game series, often expressed as a minimum, maximum, or range. Also called player count, game capacity, participant number.

label: numberOfPreviousOwners
comment: The number of owners of the vehicle, including the current one.\n\nTypical unit code(s): C62.
enriched_comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".
embedding_text: numberOfPreviousOwners: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners.

label: numberOfRooms
comment: The number of rooms (excluding bathrooms and closets) of the accommodation or lodging business. Typical unit code(s): ROM for room or C62 for no unit. The type of room can be put in the unitText property of the QuantitativeValue.
enriched_comment: The total number of rooms in an accommodation or lodging business, excluding bathrooms and closets. Also called room count, total rooms, living space rooms. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfRooms 3", "House B numberOfRooms 6", "Hotel Suite C numberOfRooms 2". Distinct from numberOfBedrooms or numberOfBathroomsTotal, which specify specific types of rooms.
embedding_text: numberOfRooms: The total number of rooms in an accommodation or lodging business, excluding bathrooms and closets. Also called room count, total rooms, living space rooms.

label: numberOfSeasons
comment: The number of seasons in this series.
enriched_comment: The total number of seasons within a radio series, TV series, or video game series. Also called season count, series seasons, total seasons. Examples: "TV Series X numberOfSeasons 10", "Radio Series Y numberOfSeasons 3", "Video Game Series Z numberOfSeasons 5". Distinct from numberOfEpisodes, which is for individual episodes within a season or series.
embedding_text: numberOfSeasons: The total number of seasons within a radio series, TV series, or video game series. Also called season count, series seasons, total seasons.

label: numberedPosition
comment: A number associated with a role in an organization, for example, the number on an athlete's jersey.
enriched_comment: A number associated with an organization role, such as an athlete's jersey number. Also called role number, position number, identifier number. Examples: "Athlete Role numberedPosition 23", "Team Member Role numberedPosition 7", "Employee Role numberedPosition 101". Distinct from namedPosition, which is a textual name for a role.
embedding_text: numberedPosition: A number associated with an organization role, such as an athlete's jersey number. Also called role number, position number, identifier number.

label: nutrition
comment: Nutrition information about the recipe or menu item.
enriched_comment: Nutrition information associated with a menu item or recipe. Also called nutritional facts, dietary information, food nutrition. Examples: "Chicken Salad MenuItem nutrition 'Calories: 350, Protein: 30g'", "Chocolate Chip Cookie Recipe nutrition 'Per serving: 150 kcal, 8g fat'", "Smoothie MenuItem nutrition 'Vitamin C: 100% DV'".
embedding_text: nutrition: Nutrition information associated with a menu item or recipe. Also called nutritional facts, dietary information, food nutrition.

label: object
comment: The object upon which the action is carried out, whose state is kept intact or changed. Also known as the semantic roles patient, affected or undergoer (which change their state) or theme (which doesn't). E.g. John read *a book*.
enriched_comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.
embedding_text: object: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action.

label: observationAbout
comment: The [[observationAbout]] property identifies an entity, often a [[Place]], associated with an [[Observation]].
enriched_comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".
embedding_text: observationAbout: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation.

label: observationDate
comment: The observationDate of an [[Observation]].
enriched_comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.
embedding_text: observationDate: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date.

label: observationPeriod
comment: The length of time an Observation took place over. The format follows `P[0-9]*[Y|M|D|h|m|s]`. For example, P1Y is Period 1 Year, P3M is Period 3 Months, P3h is Period 3 hours.
enriched_comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.
embedding_text: observationPeriod: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period.

label: occupancy
comment: The allowed total occupancy for the accommodation in persons (including infants etc). For individual accommodations, this is not necessarily the legal maximum but defines the permitted usage as per the contractual agreement (e.g. a double room used by a single person). Typical unit code(s): C62 for person.
enriched_comment: The allowed total occupancy in persons for an accommodation unit. Also called maximum occupancy, guest capacity, permitted persons. Examples: "Hotel Room occupancy 2", "Apartment occupancy 4", "Suite occupancy 6".
embedding_text: occupancy: The allowed total occupancy in persons for an accommodation unit. Also called maximum occupancy, guest capacity, permitted persons.

label: occupationLocation
comment: The region/country for which this occupational description is appropriate. Note that educational requirements and qualifications can vary between jurisdictions.
enriched_comment: An administrative area (region/country) where an occupational description is appropriate. Also called job location, employment region, occupational jurisdiction. Examples: "Software Engineer Occupation occupationLocation 'California'", "Doctor Occupation occupationLocation 'United Kingdom'", "Teacher Occupation occupationLocation 'New York State'". Distinct from workLocation, which is the specific place of work for a person.
embedding_text: occupationLocation: An administrative area (region/country) where an occupational description is appropriate. Also called job location, employment region, occupational jurisdiction.

label: occupationalCategory
comment: A category describing the job, preferably using a term from a taxonomy such as [BLS O*NET-SOC](http://www.onetcenter.org/taxonomy.html), [ISCO-08](https://www.ilo.org/public/english/bureau/stat/isco/isco08/) or similar, with the property repeated for each applicable value. Ideally the taxonomy should be identified, and both the textual label and formal code for the category should be provided.\n Note: for historical reasons, any textual label and formal code provided as a literal may be assumed to be from O*NET-SOC.
enriched_comment: A category describing a job, occupation, or educational program, often from a recognized taxonomy like O*NET-SOC or ISCO-08. Also called job category, occupation type, employment classification. Examples: "Job Posting occupationalCategory 'Software Development'", "Physician occupationalCategory 'General Practitioner'", "Work-Based Program occupationalCategory 'Construction Trades'". Distinct from industry, which is a broader classification of the economic sector.
embedding_text: occupationalCategory: A category describing a job, occupation, or educational program, often from a recognized taxonomy like O*NET-SOC or ISCO-08. Also called job category, occupation type, employment classification.

label: occupationalCredentialAwarded
comment: A description of the qualification, award, certificate, diploma or other occupational credential awarded as a consequence of successful completion of this course or program.
enriched_comment: An occupational credential, such as a qualification, award, certificate, or diploma, awarded upon successful completion of a course or program. Also called credential earned, qualification awarded, program certification. Examples: "Course X occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program Y occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Bachelor of Science'", "Training Z occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Professional Certification'". Distinct from educationalLevel, which describes the level of education attained.
embedding_text: occupationalCredentialAwarded: An occupational credential, such as a qualification, award, certificate, or diploma, awarded upon successful completion of a course or program. Also called credential earned, qualification awarded, program certification.

label: offerCount
comment: The number of offers for the product.
enriched_comment: The total number of individual offers aggregated for a product. Also called number of offers, offer quantity, total offers. Examples: "Product A AggregateOffer offerCount 10", "Service B AggregateOffer offerCount 5", "Item C AggregateOffer offerCount 20". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.
embedding_text: offerCount: The total number of individual offers aggregated for a product. Also called number of offers, offer quantity, total offers.

label: offeredBy
comment: A pointer to the organization or person making the offer.
enriched_comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.
embedding_text: offeredBy: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from.

label: offers
comment: An offer to provide this item—for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, perform a service, or give away tickets to an event. Use [[businessFunction]] to indicate the kind of transaction offered, i.e. sell, lease, etc. This property can also be used to describe a [[Demand]]. While this property is listed as expected on a number of common types, it can be used in others. In that case, using a second type, such as Product or a subtype of Product, can clarify the nature of the offer.
enriched_comment: An offer or demand related to a product, service, event, or other item. Also called available offers, related offers, product offers. Examples: "Product X offers 'Offer to sell'", "Service Y offers 'Demand for service'", "Event Z offers 'Offer for tickets'". Distinct from hasOfferCatalog, which points to a catalog of offers.
embedding_text: offers: An offer or demand related to a product, service, event, or other item. Also called available offers, related offers, product offers.

label: offersPrescriptionByMail
comment: Whether prescriptions can be delivered by mail.
enriched_comment: An indication of whether prescriptions can be delivered by mail through a health plan formulary. Also called mail-order prescriptions, prescription delivery, home delivery of meds. Examples: "Health Plan A offersPrescriptionByMail true", "Formulary B offersPrescriptionByMail false", "Insurance Plan C offersPrescriptionByMail true".
embedding_text: offersPrescriptionByMail: An indication of whether prescriptions can be delivered by mail through a health plan formulary. Also called mail-order prescriptions, prescription delivery, home delivery of meds.

label: openingHours
comment:
The general opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.

* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.
* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. 
* Here is an example: <time itemprop="openingHours" datetime="Tu,Th 16:00-20:00">Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm</time> .
* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <time itemprop="openingHours" datetime="Mo-Su">Monday through Sunday, all day</time> .
enriched_comment: A textual representation of the general opening hours for a civic structure or local business. Also called business hours, hours of operation, store hours. Examples: "Restaurant X openingHours 'Mo-Fr 09:00-17:00'", "Library Y openingHours 'Sa-Su 10:00-18:00'", "Shop Z openingHours 'Mo-Su'". Distinct from openingHoursSpecification, which uses a structured object.
embedding_text: openingHours: A textual representation of the general opening hours for a civic structure or local business. Also called business hours, hours of operation, store hours.

label: openingHoursSpecification
comment: The opening hours of a certain place.
enriched_comment: A structured specification of the opening hours for a place. Also called hours specification, detailed opening times, business hours details. Examples: "Museum A openingHoursSpecification 'OpeningHoursSpecification for Tuesday'", "Store B openingHoursSpecification 'OpeningHoursSpecification for weekends'", "Clinic C openingHoursSpecification 'OpeningHoursSpecification for holidays'". Distinct from openingHours, which is a simple text string.
embedding_text: openingHoursSpecification: A structured specification of the opening hours for a place. Also called hours specification, detailed opening times, business hours details.

label: opens
comment: The opening hour of the place or service on the given day(s) of the week.
enriched_comment: The specific time a place or service opens on a given day or days of the week. Also called opening time, start of business, daily opening hour. Examples: "Monday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '09:00'", "Weekend OpeningHoursSpecification opens '10:00'", "Weekday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '08:30'". Distinct from closes, which specifies the closing time.
embedding_text: opens: The specific time a place or service opens on a given day or days of the week. Also called opening time, start of business, daily opening hour.

label: operatingSystem
comment: Operating systems supported (Windows 7, OS X 10.6, Android 1.6).
enriched_comment: An operating system supported by a software application. Also called supported OS, compatible operating system, runs on. Examples: "Software X operatingSystem 'Windows 10'", "App Y operatingSystem 'iOS 16'", "Game Z operatingSystem 'macOS Ventura'".
embedding_text: operatingSystem: An operating system supported by a software application. Also called supported OS, compatible operating system, runs on.

label: opponent
comment: A sub property of participant. The opponent on this action.
enriched_comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.
embedding_text: opponent: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival.

label: option
comment: A sub property of object. The options subject to this action.
enriched_comment: A text or thing representing an option available for a choose action. Also called choice, alternative, selection. Examples: "Choose Meal Action option 'Chicken'", "Choose Color Action option 'Blue'", "Choose Destination Action option 'Paris'". Distinct from object, which is the general item acted upon.
embedding_text: option: A text or thing representing an option available for a choose action. Also called choice, alternative, selection.

label: orderDate
comment: Date order was placed.
enriched_comment: The date or date and time when an order was placed. Also called date of order, purchase date, transaction date. Examples: "Order 123 orderDate '2023-10-27'", "Online Purchase orderDate '2023-10-26T10:00:00'", "Subscription Order orderDate '2023-09-01'". Distinct from paymentDueDate, which is when payment is expected.
embedding_text: orderDate: The date or date and time when an order was placed. Also called date of order, purchase date, transaction date.

label: orderDelivery
comment: The delivery of the parcel related to this order or order item.
enriched_comment: A parcel delivery associated with an order or order item. Also called delivery details, shipment, parcel tracking. Examples: "Order 123 orderDelivery 'Tracking Number XYZ'", "OrderItem A orderDelivery 'Delivered by UPS'", "Purchase Order orderDelivery 'Scheduled for next week'".
embedding_text: orderDelivery: A parcel delivery associated with an order or order item. Also called delivery details, shipment, parcel tracking.

label: orderItemNumber
comment: The identifier of the order item.
enriched_comment: An identifier for a specific order item. Also called item ID, line item number, order line identifier. Examples: "OrderItem A orderItemNumber '001'", "OrderItem B orderItemNumber 'SKU-456'", "OrderItem C orderItemNumber 'LITM-789'". Distinct from orderNumber, which identifies the entire order.
embedding_text: orderItemNumber: An identifier for a specific order item. Also called item ID, line item number, order line identifier.

label: orderItemStatus
comment: The current status of the order item.
enriched_comment: The current status of an order item. Also called item status, line item status, fulfillment status. Examples: "OrderItem A orderItemStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "OrderItem B orderItemStatus 'OrderShipped'", "OrderItem C orderItemStatus 'OrderDelivered'". Distinct from orderStatus, which is for the entire order.
embedding_text: orderItemStatus: The current status of an order item. Also called item status, line item status, fulfillment status.

label: orderNumber
comment: The identifier of the transaction.
enriched_comment: An identifier for an entire order or transaction. Also called transaction ID, purchase order number, order ID. Examples: "Customer Order orderNumber 'PO-12345'", "Online Transaction orderNumber 'TXN-67890'", "Sales Order orderNumber 'SO-001'". Distinct from orderItemNumber, which identifies a specific item within an order.
embedding_text: orderNumber: An identifier for an entire order or transaction. Also called transaction ID, purchase order number, order ID.

label: orderPercentage
comment: Value representing the fraction of the value of the order that is charged as shipping cost. Example: 0.10 would mean shipping rate is 10% of the total order value.
enriched_comment: A percentage value representing the fraction of the total order value charged as shipping cost. Also called shipping cost percentage, freight percentage, delivery fee rate. Examples: "Standard Shipping orderPercentage 0.05", "Express Shipping orderPercentage 0.10", "International Shipping orderPercentage 0.15". Distinct from shippingSettingsLink, which is a URL to shipping information.
embedding_text: orderPercentage: A percentage value representing the fraction of the total order value charged as shipping cost. Also called shipping cost percentage, freight percentage, delivery fee rate.

label: orderQuantity
comment: The number of the item ordered. If the property is not set, assume the quantity is one.
enriched_comment: The number or quantity of a specific item ordered within an order item. Also called item quantity, ordered amount, number of units. Examples: "OrderItem A orderQuantity 2", "OrderItem B orderQuantity 5", "OrderItem C orderQuantity 1". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on total items for shipping.
embedding_text: orderQuantity: The number or quantity of a specific item ordered within an order item. Also called item quantity, ordered amount, number of units.

label: orderStatus
comment: The current status of the order.
enriched_comment: The current status of an entire order. Also called order state, transaction status, fulfillment state. Examples: "Order 123 orderStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "Order 456 orderStatus 'OrderDelivered'", "Order 789 orderStatus 'OrderCancelled'". Distinct from orderItemStatus, which is for individual items within an order.
embedding_text: orderStatus: The current status of an entire order. Also called order state, transaction status, fulfillment state.

label: orderValue
comment: Minimum and maximum order value for which these shipping conditions are valid.
enriched_comment: A monetary amount representing the minimum or maximum order value for which specific shipping conditions are valid. Also called order total threshold, shipping value limit, purchase amount condition. Examples: "Free Shipping orderValue '$50.00'", "Discounted Shipping orderValue 'min $100.00'", "Special Rate Shipping orderValue 'max $20.00'". Distinct from orderPercentage, which is a rate based on order value.
embedding_text: orderValue: A monetary amount representing the minimum or maximum order value for which specific shipping conditions are valid. Also called order total threshold, shipping value limit, purchase amount condition.

label: orderedItem
comment: The item ordered.
enriched_comment: An item (product, service, or another order item) that has been ordered. Also called purchased item, item in order, ordered product. Examples: "Order 123 orderedItem 'Laptop X'", "OrderItem A orderedItem 'Software License'", "Subscription Order orderedItem 'Premium Service'".
embedding_text: orderedItem: An item (product, service, or another order item) that has been ordered. Also called purchased item, item in order, ordered product.

label: organizer
comment: An organizer of an Event.
enriched_comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.
embedding_text: organizer: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter.

label: originAddress
comment: Shipper's address.
enriched_comment: The postal address of the shipper for a parcel delivery. Also called shipper address, sender's address, dispatch address. Examples: "Parcel Delivery 1 originAddress '123 Main St, Anytown'", "Shipment 2 originAddress 'Warehouse A, City B'", "Package 3 originAddress 'Sender's Home, Zip 12345'". Distinct from deliveryAddress, which is the recipient's address.
embedding_text: originAddress: The postal address of the shipper for a parcel delivery. Also called shipper address, sender's address, dispatch address.

label: originalMediaContextDescription
comment: Describes, in a [[MediaReview]] when dealing with [[DecontextualizedContent]], background information that can contribute to better interpretation of the [[MediaObject]].
enriched_comment: Background information that aids in better interpretation of a media object, especially for decontextualized content in a media review. Also called media context, original context, background description. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaContextDescription 'Video was originally posted on TikTok in 2020.'", "Image Review B originalMediaContextDescription 'Photo taken during a protest in 2018, not current event.'", "Audio Review C originalMediaContextDescription 'Clip is from a satirical podcast, not a news broadcast.'". Distinct from reviewBody, which is the main text of the review.
embedding_text: originalMediaContextDescription: Background information that aids in better interpretation of a media object, especially for decontextualized content in a media review. Also called media context, original context, background description.

label: originalMediaLink
comment: Link to the page containing an original version of the content, or directly to an online copy of the original [[MediaObject]] content, e.g. video file.
enriched_comment: A link to the original version of media content, such as a web page or a direct media object file, in a media review. Also called source media link, original content URL, primary media source. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaLink 'https://originalsource.com/video123'", "Image Review B originalMediaLink 'https://archive.org/image456'", "Audio Review C originalMediaLink 'https://podcast.example.com/episode789'". Distinct from url, which is the URL of the review itself.
embedding_text: originalMediaLink: A link to the original version of media content, such as a web page or a direct media object file, in a media review. Also called source media link, original content URL, primary media source.

label: originatesFrom
comment: The vasculature the lymphatic structure originates, or afferents, from.
enriched_comment: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel. Examples: "Lymphatic Vessel A originatesFrom 'Capillary Bed X'", "Thoracic Duct originatesFrom 'Cisterna Chyli'", "Lymphatic Capillary originatesFrom 'Interstitial Fluid'". Distinct from runsTo, which describes the destination.
embedding_text: originatesFrom: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel.

label: overdosage
comment: Any information related to overdose on a drug, including signs or symptoms, treatments, contact information for emergency response.
enriched_comment: Information related to drug overdose, including signs, symptoms, treatments, and emergency contact details. Also called overdose information, toxicity details, emergency overdose guidance. Examples: "Drug X overdosage 'Symptoms include nausea and dizziness. Contact poison control immediately.'", "Medication Y overdosage 'Administer activated charcoal. Seek urgent medical attention.'", "Supplement Z overdosage 'May cause liver damage in high doses.'". Distinct from sideEffect, which describes adverse effects at normal doses.
embedding_text: overdosage: Information related to drug overdose, including signs, symptoms, treatments, and emergency contact details. Also called overdose information, toxicity details, emergency overdose guidance.

label: ownedFrom
comment: The date and time of obtaining the product.
enriched_comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.
embedding_text: ownedFrom: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired.

label: ownedThrough
comment: The date and time of giving up ownership on the product.
enriched_comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2023-05-20'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2022-11-30T16:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2024-01-01'". Distinct from ownedFrom, which is the date ownership began.
embedding_text: ownedThrough: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date.

label: owner
comment: A person or organization who owns this Thing.
enriched_comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.
embedding_text: owner: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder.

label: ownershipFundingInfo
comment: For an [[Organization]] (often but not necessarily a [[NewsMediaOrganization]]), a description of organizational ownership structure; funding and grants. In a news/media setting, this is with particular reference to editorial independence. Note that the [[funder]] is also available and can be used to make basic funder information machine-readable.
enriched_comment: Information describing the ownership structure, funding, and grants of an organization, particularly concerning editorial independence for news media. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure, financial backing details. Examples: "News Org A ownershipFundingInfo 'https://news.example.com/about/funding'", "Company B ownershipFundingInfo 'Privately held by XYZ Group.'", "Nonprofit C ownershipFundingInfo 'Funded by grants from various foundations.'". Distinct from funder, which specifically identifies the entity providing funds.
embedding_text: ownershipFundingInfo: Information describing the ownership structure, funding, and grants of an organization, particularly concerning editorial independence for news media. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure, financial backing details.

label: owns
comment: Things owned by the organization or person.
enriched_comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.
embedding_text: owns: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of.

label: pageEnd
comment: The page on which the work ends; for example "138" or "xvi".
enriched_comment: The page number or identifier where a work (article, chapter, etc.) concludes. Also called ending page, last page, final page number. Examples: "Article X pageEnd 138", "Chapter Y pageEnd 'xvi'", "Report Z pageEnd 25". Distinct from pageStart, which is the beginning page. pagination is a general range.
embedding_text: pageEnd: The page number or identifier where a work (article, chapter, etc.) concludes. Also called ending page, last page, final page number.

label: pageStart
comment: The page on which the work starts; for example "135" or "xiii".
enriched_comment: The page number or identifier where a work (article, chapter, etc.) begins. Also called starting page, first page, initial page number. Examples: "Article X pageStart 135", "Chapter Y pageStart 'xiii'", "Report Z pageStart 1". Distinct from pageEnd, which is the concluding page. pagination is a general range.
embedding_text: pageStart: The page number or identifier where a work (article, chapter, etc.) begins. Also called starting page, first page, initial page number.

label: pagination
comment: Any description of pages that is not separated into pageStart and pageEnd; for example, "1-6, 9, 55" or "10-12, 46-49".
enriched_comment: A textual description of page numbers or ranges for a work, not separated into distinct start and end properties. Also called page range, page numbering, page sequence. Examples: "Article X pagination '1-6, 9, 55'", "Chapter Y pagination '10-12, 46-49'", "Journal Entry Z pagination 'pp. 20-25'". Distinct from pageStart and pageEnd, which are specific start and end points.
embedding_text: pagination: A textual description of page numbers or ranges for a work, not separated into distinct start and end properties. Also called page range, page numbering, page sequence.

label: parent
comment: A parent of this person.
enriched_comment: A person who is a parent of another person. Also called mother, father, progenitor. Examples: "Child A parent 'Parent B'", "Person X parent 'Mother Y'", "Person Z parent 'Father W'". Distinct from children, which describes the offspring.
embedding_text: parent: A person who is a parent of another person. Also called mother, father, progenitor.

label: parentItem
comment: The parent of a question, answer or item in general. Typically used for Q/A discussion threads e.g. a chain of comments with the first comment being an [[Article]] or other [[CreativeWork]]. See also [[comment]] which points from something to a comment about it.
enriched_comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.
embedding_text: parentItem: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to.

label: parentOrganization
comment: The larger organization that this organization is a [[subOrganization]] of, if any.
enriched_comment: A hierarchical relation between an organization and the larger organization it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is a division of, is a subsidiary of, is part of. Examples: Google is a parent organization of YouTube. A local branch is a parent organization of its national headquarters. A department is a parent organization of its university. Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a larger organization to its smaller components.
embedding_text: parentOrganization: A hierarchical relation between an organization and the larger organization it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is a division of, is a subsidiary of, is part of.

label: parentService
comment: A broadcast service to which the broadcast service may belong to such as regional variations of a national channel.
enriched_comment: A hierarchical relation between a broadcast service and a broader broadcast service it is a variation or component of. Also called belongs to, is a variation of, is part of, is a channel of. Examples: BBC One Scotland is a parent service of BBC One. A regional news channel is a parent service of a national news channel. A specific sports channel is a parent service of a broader sports network.
embedding_text: parentService: A hierarchical relation between a broadcast service and a broader broadcast service it is a variation or component of. Also called belongs to, is a variation of, is part of, is a channel of.

label: parentTaxon
comment: Closest parent taxon of the taxon in question.
enriched_comment: A taxonomic relation between a taxon and its immediate higher-level taxon. Also called is a sub-taxon of, belongs to the taxon, is classified under. Examples: Homo is a parent taxon of Homo sapiens. Felidae is a parent taxon of Panthera. Mammalia is a parent taxon of Primates.
embedding_text: parentTaxon: A taxonomic relation between a taxon and its immediate higher-level taxon. Also called is a sub-taxon of, belongs to the taxon, is classified under.

label: parents
comment: A parents of the person.
enriched_comment: A familial relation between a person and their biological or adoptive parents. Also called is a child of, has as a parent, is parented by. Examples: John is a parent of Mary. Jane is a parent of David. The parents of a child are their mother and father. Distinct from children, which points from a parent to their offspring.
embedding_text: parents: A familial relation between a person and their biological or adoptive parents. Also called is a child of, has as a parent, is parented by.

label: partOfEpisode
comment: The episode to which this clip belongs.
enriched_comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.
embedding_text: partOfEpisode: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from.

label: partOfInvoice
comment: The order is being paid as part of the referenced Invoice.
enriched_comment: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by. Examples: An online purchase order is part of an invoice. A service request order is part of an invoice. Multiple orders can be part of a single invoice.
embedding_text: partOfInvoice: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by.

label: partOfOrder
comment: The overall order the items in this delivery were included in.
enriched_comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.
embedding_text: partOfOrder: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in.

label: partOfSeason
comment: The season to which this episode belongs.
enriched_comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.
embedding_text: partOfSeason: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of.

label: partOfSeries
comment: The series to which this episode or season belongs.
enriched_comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.
embedding_text: partOfSeries: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of.

label: partOfSystem
comment: The anatomical or organ system that this structure is part of.
enriched_comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

label: price
comment:
The offer price of a product, or of a price component when attached to PriceSpecification and its subtypes.

Usage guidelines:

* Use the [[priceCurrency]] property (with standard formats: [ISO 4217 currency format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217), e.g. "USD"; [Ticker symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cryptocurrencies) for cryptocurrencies, e.g. "BTC"; well known names for [Local Exchange Trading Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_exchange_trading_system) (LETS) and other currency types, e.g. "Ithaca HOUR") instead of including [ambiguous symbols](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollar_sign#Currencies_that_use_the_dollar_or_peso_sign) such as '$' in the value.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
* Note that both [RDFa](http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml-rdfa-primer/#using-the-content-attribute) and Microdata syntax allow the use of a "content=" attribute for publishing simple machine-readable values alongside more human-friendly formatting.
* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
enriched_comment: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount. Examples: An offer has a price of '19.99'. A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.
embedding_text: price: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount.

Examples: A compound price specification includes a price component for 'base rate'. The total price has a price component for 'tax'. The invoice lists a price component for 'shipping fee'.
embedding_text: priceComponent: A compositional relation between a compound price specification and its individual unit price components. Also called price breakdown, cost element, pricing detail.

Examples: A unit price specification has a price component type of 'BasePrice'. A price component has a price component type of 'Tax'. A line item has a price component type of 'ShippingFee'.
embedding_text: priceComponentType: A categorical attribute identifying the specific type of a price component, such as a line item on an invoice. Also called component type, charge type, fee category.

comment: A commonly used identifier for the characteristic represented by the property, e.g. a manufacturer or a standard code for a property. propertyID can be (1) a prefixed string, mainly meant to be used with standards for product properties; (2) a site-specific, non-prefixed string (e.g. the primary key of the property or the vendor-specific ID of the property), or (3) a URL indicating the type of the property, either pointing to an external vocabulary, or a Web resource that describes the property (e.g. a glossary entry). Standards bodies should promote a standard prefix for the identifiers of properties from their standards.
enriched_comment: An identifier relation between a property value and a standard or site-specific code representing the characteristic. Also called characteristic ID, standard code, vendor ID. Examples: "A product's color property has a propertyID 'RAL 5010'.", "A material's hardness property has a propertyID 'Mohs 7'.", "A dimension property has a propertyID 'ISO 2768-1'."
embedding_text: propertyID: An identifier relation between a property value and a standard or site-specific code representing the characteristic. Also called characteristic ID, standard code, vendor ID.

label: proprietaryName

label: publishingPrinciples
comment: The publishingPrinciples property indicates (typically via [[URL]]) a document describing the editorial principles of an [[Organization]] (or individual, e.g. a [[Person]] writing a blog) that relate to their activities as a publisher, e.g. ethics or diversity policies. While such policies are most typically expressed in natural language, sometimes related information (e.g. indicating a [[funder]]) can be expressed using schema.org terminology.

embedding_text: publishingPrinciples: A publishing principles relation between a creative work, organization, or person and the document outlining their editorial and ethical guidelines as a publisher. Also called editorial guidelines, ethics policy, publishing policy.

label: purchaseDate

label: ratingValue
comment:
The rating for the content.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

label: speakable
comment: Indicates sections of a Web page that are particularly 'speakable' in the sense of being highlighted as being especially appropriate for text-to-speech conversion. Other sections of a page may also be usefully spoken in particular circumstances; the 'speakable' property serves to indicate the parts most likely to be generally useful for speech. The *speakable* property can be repeated an arbitrary number of times, with three kinds of possible 'content-locator' values: 1.) *id-value* URL references - uses *id-value* of an element in the page being annotated. The simplest use of *speakable* has (potentially relative) URL values, referencing identified sections of the document concerned. 2.) CSS Selectors - addresses content in the annotated page, e.g. via class attribute. Use the [[cssSelector]] property. 3.) XPaths - addresses content via XPaths (assuming an XML view of the content). Use the [[xpath]] property. For more sophisticated markup of speakable sections beyond simple ID references, either CSS selectors or XPath expressions to pick out document section(s) as speakable. For this we define a supporting type, [[SpeakableSpecification]] which is defined to be a possible value of the *speakable* property.

label: usageInfo
comment: The schema.org [[usageInfo]] property indicates further information about a [[CreativeWork]]. This property is applicable both to works that are freely available and to those that require payment or other transactions. It can reference additional information, e.g. community expectations on preferred linking and citation conventions, as well as purchasing details. For something that can be commercially licensed, usageInfo can provide detailed, resource-specific information about licensing options. This property can be used alongside the license property which indicates license(s) applicable to some piece of content. The usageInfo property can provide information about other licensing options, e.g. acquiring commercial usage rights for an image that is also available under non-commercial creative commons licenses.
enriched_comment: A usage info relation between a creative work and additional information about its use, including licensing options, citation conventions, or purchasing details. Also called usage guidelines, licensing information, rights information. Examples: "CreativeWork usageInfo 'https://example.com/usage-policy'", "Image usageInfo 'Commercial licenses available upon request.'", "Dataset usageInfo 'https://example.com/data-license'". Distinct from license, which indicates the specific license(s) applicable to the content.
embedding_text: usageInfo: A usage info relation between a creative work and additional information about its use, including licensing options, citation conventions, or purchasing details. Also called usage guidelines, licensing information, rights information.

embedding_text: usedToDiagnose: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for.

label: value
comment:
The value of a [[QuantitativeValue]] (including [[Observation]]) or property value node.

* For [[QuantitativeValue]] and [[MonetaryAmount]], the recommended type for values is 'Number'.
* For [[PropertyValue]], it can be 'Text', 'Number', 'Boolean', or 'StructuredValue'.
* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
enriched_comment: A value relation between a monetary amount, property value, or quantitative value and its specific numerical, textual, boolean, or structured content. Also called amount, quantity, content. Examples: "QuantitativeValue value '10'", "PropertyValue value 'red'", "MonetaryAmount value '99.99'".
embedding_text: value: A value relation between a monetary amount, property value, or quantitative value and its specific numerical, textual, boolean, or structured content. Also called amount, quantity, content.

embedding_text: valueAddedTaxIncluded: A value-added tax included relation between a price specification and whether VAT is part of the price. Also called VAT status, tax inclusion, includes VAT.

embedding_text: vatID: A VAT ID relation between an organization or person and their value-added Tax ID with a national prefix. Also called VAT number, tax identification number, sales tax ID.

label: workFeatured

embedding_text: workFeatured: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work.
